text:
Connor O'Brien: heads up: aiming to cut runtime-1.19 tomorrow (Thu) EOD PT. Need to align on selector v2 staged rollout checklist + what has to be in the cut vs can land post-cut.

Key q’s:
1) what’s our go/no-go criteria for enabling v2 canary in us-east?
2) who’s signing off (runtime + SRE) and when?
3) are we comfortable shipping the flag + kill switch in 1.19 even if default remains v1?

Link to checklist doc (draft): https://drive.google.com/.../kernel-selector-v2-rollout-checklist

Marissa Cole: +1. For rollout sequencing I’m tracking: internal canary -> 5% hosted us-east -> 25% hosted us-east -> expand regions -> dedicated opt-in -> default-on later.

But release notes need to be explicit that it’s behind a flag and not customer-visible unless enabled.

Talia Benson: re: schedule, I can herd sign-offs but need a crisp list of prereqs. Right now doc has a lot of “nice to have” monitors.

Can we agree on the minimal set of dashboards + alerts we require before flipping 5%?

Benji Okafor: runtime config side: flag + kill switch is in pr_18480 and pr_18558 (docs + precedence). Both are merged to main; cherry-pick is clean.

Current config keys (names final):
- `runtime.kernel_selector.version = v1|v2`
- `runtime.kernel_selector.v2.enabled = true|false`
- `runtime.kernel_selector.v2.emergency_disable = true|false` (takes precedence)
- `runtime.kernel_selector.overrides.model_family.* = <kernel_id>` (optional)

So shipping 1.19 with defaults still v1 is fine.

Grace Kim: from runtime side, I’d really like pr_18571 (seq bucket off-by-one) included in 1.19 cut. That bug shows up in benchmark sweep at the bucket boundary and it’s hard to reason about canary deltas if bucket labels are wrong.

Also pr_18526 (unknown model family safe fallback) should be in. That was the rare crash in early canary.

Hiro Tanaka: +1 to Grace. Those two are “must”.

“nice to have” for cut: pr_18519 (cardinality reduction) if it’s low risk. But we can also ship it in 1.19.1.

Sahana Iyer: perf-canary gate status as of this morning:
- selector v2 on: PASS on A100/H100/L4, borderline on A10 long-context (still within threshold after the latest fix)
- selector v1 baseline: PASS

CI link: https://perf-canary.redwood/.../runs/388-2217

Acceptance criteria we encoded (current): p95 must not regress >3% on any GPU bucket for the “mixed” workload suite, and >5% allowed only if cost/token improves >=5% (rare). Happy to tighten later.

Aisha Bello: SRE side: I want one more thing before flipping even 5%:
- dashboard panel for selector version breakdown + kernel-choice heatmap (INT-2331)
- alert that pages on p95 + error rate for the canary cohort only (so we’re not paging on global noise)

We can do without the heatmap for day 1 but we do need the version breakdown + cohort scoping.

Allison Grant: +1. Also please ensure telemetry labels are bucketed (seq bucket not raw seq len, gpu_sku normalized) so we don’t blow cardinality when we enable.

If pr_18519 isn’t in the cut, confirm that the metrics label set is already compliant with the standards doc.

Grace Kim: label set is already bucketed in pr_18493; pr_18519 is basically “reduce one dimension + adjust aggregation” after we saw cardinality growth in staging. It’s safer to have it, but not strictly required if we keep sampling at 1% for per-kernel breakdown.

Sana Farid: canary analysis checklist request: can we put explicit “compare v1 vs v2 within same cohort” instructions in the doc?

Last time we got burned because overall p95 moved due to traffic mix changes. Need:
- same region
- same model family (at least top 3)
- same seq bucket
- split by GPU

If we do that, 5% is fine.

Connor O'Brien: ok, proposing:

**Must be in runtime-1.19 cut**
- seq bucket off-by-one fix (pr_18571)
- unknown model family safe fallback (pr_18526)
- feature flag + kill switch + override precedence docs (pr_18480 + pr_18558)

**Strongly preferred in cut**
- telemetry cardinality reduction (pr_18519)

**Not required for cut**
- canary config enablement pr (we can apply via config repo after 1.19 is in prod)

Does anyone object?

Hiro Tanaka: no objection.

Grace Kim: works for me.

Allison Grant: ok if we commit to doing the cardinality reduction before we go past 5%. Otherwise we’ll be chasing metrics once 25% hits.

Aisha Bello: agree. Also: we need a clean rollback path documented. The runbook should state exactly which knob to flip and what “good” looks like after rollback.

Benji Okafor: rollback is “set `runtime.kernel_selector.v2.emergency_disable=true`” (or just set version to v1 globally). Propagation time ~2-3 mins via config push. We can add a “verify” step:
- selector_version metric goes back to v1
- kernel_choice distribution matches baseline
- p95 returns within 10 mins

Talia Benson: can someone assign owners for each gate?
- perf-canary green: Sahana
- dashboards + alerts: Aisha
- telemetry label compliance: Allison (or Thomas, but he’s not on this thread)
- runtime correctness/conformance suite: Grace/Hiro
- final go/no-go: Connor + runtime EM + SRE on-call

Connor O'Brien: yep. Let’s do:
- Sahana: perf-canary green + link
- Aisha: dashboard panel + scoped alert
- Grace/Hiro: confirm conformance tests green on release branch
- Benji: confirm kill switch wiring + precedence in release notes
- Sana: canary analysis template section in checklist

I’ll own coordinating the actual cut + cherry-picks.

DeployBot: `runtime-main` build #11942 succeeded. Artifact: `runtime-1.19.0-rc1` available. Commit: 8f3c2a9.

Connor O'Brien: I’m going to start the cherry-pick set for rc2:
- 18571
- 18526
- 18519 (if it applies cleanly)

If conflicts, I’ll drop 18519 and we’ll do 1.19.1.

Marissa Cole: rollout comms: please include a one-liner in the internal release note like “Kernel selector v2 shipped behind flag; no default behavior change.”

Also for dedicated customers, we should be explicit it’s opt-in only and needs SRE approval for first few.

Aisha Bello: re: scoped alerting, I can do a canary cohort label based on `selector_version=v2` + region=us-east + tier=hosted. That should isolate.

Question: do we have a separate “canary enablement” label in config that shows up in metrics? Otherwise distinguishing accidental v2 usage vs intentional cohort might be hard.

Benji Okafor: not currently. We can add `selector_rollout_cohort` label, but that’s new cardinality. Alternative: encode via config name / region and rely on selector_version + region. If we need explicit cohort, we can add as a config-only log field in traces rather than metric label.

Allison Grant: please don’t add cohort as a metric label right now. Use selector_version + region + tier and sampling.

Sana Farid: for analysis, selector_version + region + gpu_sku + model_family + seq_bucket is enough. We can get rollout cohort from the config PR / deployment window.

Sahana Iyer: FYI the A10 long-context borderline mentioned earlier was tied to one kernel choice in the registry. With seq bucket fix, the distribution is cleaner. So +1 to getting 18571 in.

Grace Kim: conformance tests are green on main after 18501; I’ll re-run on the release branch once Connor has rc2. There was that NaN edge case previously; now guarded by “safe kernel set” fallback.

Connor O'Brien: great. Timeline:
- I’ll cut rc2 in ~2 hours.
- Aisha to land dashboard panel by EOD.
- Tomorrow morning PT: 15 min go/no-go (Connor + Aisha + Grace + Sahana + Sana). If green, we cut 1.19 and schedule config change for 5% us-east after lunch.

Sound ok?

Aisha Bello: ok.

Grace Kim: ok.

Sana Farid: works.

DeployBot: `runtime-release/1.19` build #11958 succeeded. Artifact: `runtime-1.19.0-rc2` available. Commit: 4c1a0d7. Cherry-picks: 18571, 18526, 18519.

Connor O'Brien: rc2 is out w/ 18519 included (nice). Please validate:
- dashboards/alerts
- conformance
- perf-canary still green

If no surprises, we ship 1.19 tomorrow and proceed w/ 5% config PR.

:thumbsup: (reactions from Marissa Cole, Talia Benson, Hiro Tanaka)
